title: Applied ML Evals — Cross-functional Playbook: Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook documents the cross-functional process used by Applied ML, Eval Engineering, and Runtime teams for: model onboarding into the eval harness, prompt set and benchmark management, generation of quantization profiles, and regression triage. The goal is to make model rollouts predictable and to ensure quality regressions are detected, triaged, and remediated with clear ownership and SLAs.

Scope

- Models and model variants submitted for serving (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Prompt sets and benchmarks used for production quality monitoring and release gates.
- Quantization profile generation and validation for supported hardware targets.
- Regression triage process from alert to resolution.

Out of scope

- Research experiments that are not intended for serving.
- Ad-hoc manual prompt experiments that are not registered in the prompt-set catalog.

Ownership and roles

- Applied ML / Eval Engineering: maintain the eval harness, prompt-set catalog, baseline metrics, and regression triage lead.
- Serving Runtime: owns quantization tooling, kernel selection, and performance validation.
- Platform / SRE: owns CI gating, rollout automation, and incident communication channels.
- Product / Solutions: provides product-oriented acceptance criteria and customer-specific test sets where applicable.

Definitions

- Eval Harness: the automated system that runs unit, integration and behavioral tests against candidate models and variants.
- Prompt-set: curated set of input-output pairs used to evaluate specific product behaviors (e.g., summarization, codegen, retrieval-augmented responses).
- Quantization Profile: a parameterized configuration (dtype, per-channel/per-tensor, calibration set) used to produce a quantized model build targeted at specific hardware.
- Regression Alert: automated evaluation signal that a model variant dropped below an accepted threshold on one or more metrics.

Pre-onboarding checklist (required before model is added to eval harness)

1. Model card completed with architecture, training data summary, license, and declared limitations.
2. Initial FP16 (or better) reference build validated locally by model owner.
3. Suggested prompt-sets mapped to product surfaces (see Prompt-set catalog).
4. Quantization compatibility verification: model has supported ops for our quantizer (see quantization-profiles guide).
5. Baseline metric snapshot created from evaluation on the core prompt-sets.

Model onboarding (step-by-step)

1. Create a model entry in the model registry with metadata: version, architecture, training checkpoints, owner, and intended use-cases.
2. Add the model to the eval harness job definition with target prompt-sets and performance metrics.
3. Run baseline suite (core prompt-sets + safety checks + performance microbenchmarks). Expected outputs: baseline metrics JSON, latency p50/p95, memory footprint.
4. If baseline passes, trigger quantization profile generation (see Quantization profiling).
5. Validate quantized variant(s) against baseline prompt-sets and extra product-specific tests.
6. Approve model for staged rollout (canary) if quality thresholds are met.

Eval harness integration checklist

- Required outputs from each job: metrics.json, failure-summary.txt, sample-responses/<n>.json, and perf-report.csv.
- CI gating rule: no metric should regress beyond configured thresholds (see Gating thresholds).
- All runs must be reproducible with the same random seed and dataset snapshot id recorded.

Gating thresholds (default)

- Behavioral metrics (task-specific accuracy, ROUGE, BLEU, F1): no >5% relative drop vs baseline unless product signoff.
- Hallucination rate (measured on curated set): absolute increase must be <= 2 percentage points.
- Latency: p95 must not increase >20% for dedicated targets; absolute p95 target depends on model class (see Performance SLOs table).
- Embedding cosine similarity (for embedding tasks): average decrease must be <= 0.02.

Prompt-set management

- Ownership: each prompt-set must have an owner and a short description specifying the behavior tested, expected outputs, and tolerance.
- Versioning: prompt-sets are immutable once used for a release gate; version increments for updates and regeneration.
- Catalog fields: id, name, owner, product_surface, sample_count, labels (safety, hallucination, codegen, summarization), dataset_source, last_updated.
- Review cadence: quarterly review for high-usage prompt-sets; immediate review triggered by customer incidents or significant model changes.

Quantization profiling and profiles

Purpose: generate quantized model variants that balance unit cost with acceptable quality degradation. Process: run automated per-layer sensitivity analysis, select calibration set (representative prompt-set), generate candidate profiles, and run round-trip validation.

Profile selection checklist:

1. Choose calibration prompt-set: 500-2,000 representative examples covering target distributions.
2. Run per-layer MSE and kl-divergence sensitivity analysis.
3. Classify layers into buckets: safe-to-4bit, safe-to-8bit, require-fp16.
4. Generate candidate profiles (int8/4bit mixed, group-wise quantization where supported).
5. Validate candidates against prompt-set catalog with gating thresholds.

Recommended profiles (example table):

| profile_id | target_hw | quant_type | expected_quality_delta | recommended_use_cases | notes |
|-----------|-----------|------------|------------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| q-profile-h100-int8 | H100 | mixed-int8 (per-channel) | ~0-1% relative on task accuracy | high-throughput batch inference | default for latency-sensitive batch jobs |
| q-profile-a100-int8 | A100 | per-tensor int8 | ~1-2% relative | dedicated serving where throughput matters | verify attention kernel coverage |
| q-profile-t4-int8 | T4 | per-tensor int8 with fallback | ~2-4% relative | low-cost inference; smaller seq len | expected higher latency for long seqs |
| q-profile-mixed-4bit | H100/A100 | mixed 4-bit (group-wise) | ~3-6% relative | experimental cost-optimized builds | require additional safety checks |

Note: expected_quality_delta is empirical and depends on model architecture and task; always validate on product prompt-sets.

Validation artifacts to collect:

- metrics.json (per-profile), diff_vs_baseline.json, sample-response-diffs/*.json, perf.csv (throughput, p50, p95), mem-usage.txt.

CI gating example (YAML snippet)

```yaml
jobs:
  run-evals:
    runs-on: runners/eval-large
    steps:
      - checkout
      - run: eval-harness run --model $MODEL --profiles default,quantized
      - run: eval-harness compare --baseline baseline_metrics.json --candidate metrics.json --thresholds gating.yaml
```

Regression triage playbook (fast path)

1. Detection: Alert generated by the eval-harness or monitoring (metric drift, failing release gate, customer-reported regression).
2. Triage lead (Applied ML) acknowledges within 1 business hour for P1/P2; documents initial impact and affected prompt-sets.
3. Reproduce: run deterministic eval harness job with same dataset snapshot id. Attach artifacts.
4. Classify regression: data, model, quantization, serving (infrastructure), prompt drift.
5. Hotfix actions (based on classification):
   - Model bug: roll back to previous approved variant and open a model-fix PR.
   - Quantization regression: fall back to FP16 variant for the affected deployment or use alternate quant profile.
   - Prompt drift or dataset issue: revert prompt set or update test expectations with product signoff.
   - Serving regression: engage runtime and SRE for perf remediation.
6. Communication: update incident channel with status every 2 hours until mitigated for P1; create postmortem for P1/P2 within 7 days.

Severity definitions and SLAs

- P1 (Service-impacting quality regression): large production impact (e.g., >10% drop in critical accuracy metric or >5pt BLEU/ROUGE change). Acknowledgement within 1 hour; mitigation within 8 hours OR rollback.
- P2 (Material regression): measurable impact on users (e.g., 5-10% drop). Acknowledgement within 4 hours; mitigation plan within 48 hours.
- P3 (Minor): localized test failures or non-customer-facing regressions. Acknowledgement within 2 business days.

Postmortem and continuous improvement

- For all P1/P2 incidents create a postmortem template entry with: root cause, timeline, remediation, owner for preventative work, and action items with due dates.
- Quarterly review of regression origins to prioritize engineering work (quantizer improvements, kernel coverage, prompt-set expansion).

Operational runbook (quick reference)

1. If a release gate fails during CI: halt rollout; notify rollout owner; run detailed diff job (eval-harness compare --verbose).
2. If production alerts indicate degraded quality: open incident, instantiate triage lead, start fast-path triage.
3. For quantization-specific failures: toggle to FP16 variant via routing policy and mark quant profile as suspended pending investigation.

Key metrics to monitor continuously

- Release-gate pass rate (daily, weekly).
- Regression alerts per 100 model-deployments.
- Average time-to-mitigate for P1/P2.
- Quantized vs FP16 quality delta distributions by model family.

Appendix: example sensitivity analysis command

```
# run per-layer sensitivity and generate candidate profiles
quant-tool analyze --model-path model.fp16.pt --calib-set calib_manifest.json --out profiles/ --per-layer-metrics
quant-tool generate --profiles profiles/ --target hw=a100,group_bits=4,8 --out builds/
```
